newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish debt yields end down on CPI, deficit data.
newsitem.headline: Swedish debt yields end down on CPI, deficit data.

text.p: Lower-than-expected CPI figures and a reduction in the state budget deficit forecast for the 18 month 1995/96 fiscal period fuelled a fall in Swedish debt yields on Thursday.

The crown weakened against the mark in the morning but strengthened some after the CPI figures. Dealers would be focusing on the Dublin summit on Friday, they said. * Six-month T-bill rates fall twelve basis points to 3.92 pct * Ten-year bond yields drop six basis points to 6.94 pct * Crown weakens to 4.4100 against mark vs 4.4065 Wednesday
STOCKHOLM, Dec 12 (Reuter) - Swedish debt yields took a strong fall on Thursday after positive consumer price index (CPI) figures and a revised, lower forecast of the budget deficit were announced.
Statistics Sweden posted a 0.3 percent fall in consumer prices in November from October for an annualised fall of 0.3 percent. The market had expected a fall of 0.1 percent.
Dealers said that the CPI made the market even more convinced of the Riksbank's intention to lower its key interest rate, the repo rate on December 17 from its current level of 4.35 percent.
"The market is expecting a repo rate cut of 25 basis points. That made the T-bill rates fall considerably. There are no reasons to sell," one dealer said.
The six-month T-bill rate dropped 12 basis points to 3.92 percent and the ten-year bond yield fell six to 6.94 percent.
The crown weakened to 4.4100 crowns against the mark compared to 4.4065 late Wednesday.
Dealers said the main focus on Friday was the ECOFIN-meeting and the Dublin summit. "The big threat to the markets now is Friday the 13th," one dealer said.
